topics.title: Content
topics.summary: Reuse pages, posts and structured entries as the site data model.
topics.explanation: A directory starts with a content type and entries, not hardcoded profile cards in a theme. Choose fields from real requirements, discover the current content-type tools, and distinguish draft from published records. Render the same data in lists and pages. Public entry-page routing may require an additional capability; verify it rather than assuming every content type has its own public URL.

workflows.title: Design the directory data model
steps: Explain forms and widgets before choosing the schema.
Inspect existing content types and entries.
Propose the fields and publishing policy; discover the actual create/update tool schemas before editing.

topics.title: Forms
topics.summary: Use native forms for inquiries, contact requests and submissions.
topics.explanation: A form definition owns validation, persistence and submission handling. A contact-form widget references that definition; it does not create another submission pipeline. Theme/page HTML uses a data-embed-config form marker. Read live fieldTypes first; richer fields are not supported merely because HTML can render them. Forms created from authored HTML have their own contract: inspect the forms authoring tools before assuming definition fields and markup are interchangeable.

workflows.title: Add a planner inquiry form
steps: Read the live fieldTypes and describe forms_create_definition.
Reuse or create a definition with supported fields.
Explain widgets; reference the form id in a contact-form widget or a form marker.
Preview the rendered form and verify its public submit path.

topics.title: Widgets
topics.summary: Reuse widget instances and theme regions to compose pages.
topics.explanation: A widget instance is reusable content with a registered type/config schema. Creating it does not place it. Regions hold placements; an inline marker embeds an existing instance. Read current region versions before replacing placements. Contact forms reference native form definitions, recent-entry widgets reference real content, and unknown widget types must not be invented. A directory that needs filtering must verify a registered filtering capability before proposing it.

workflows.title: Place a reusable inquiry widget
steps: Explain forms and reuse the form definition id.
Describe widgets_create_instance and create a contact-form instance.
Read the intended region and its version; replace placements only after preserving the other widgets.
Preview the page at desktop and 375px.

topics.title: Themes
topics.summary: Use the active theme contracts, layouts and markers.
topics.explanation: Themes present site content; they do not own form persistence, member authorization or content CRUD. Before creating pages or themes, load the ui-ux-design skill first with agent_plugin_ui_ux_design({"skill":"ui-ux-design"}) and follow its guidance. Read installed/active theme facts and the current marker/layout registry. A single-quoted data-embed-config attribute carries JSON describing an existing content, form, widget, menu or partial target. Use only reported marker types. Duplicate the theme, inspect its actual files and preview changes before the owner approves activation. Ask the host for another plugin capability rather than importing another plugin.

workflows.title: Compose a directory theme
steps: Explain content, forms and widgets.
Inspect the selected theme layout and existing regions.
Work in a duplicated theme; use native embeds rather than reimplementing submission logic.
Preview at desktop and 375px; ask before activation.

topics.title: Members
topics.summary: Separate visitor membership from administrator/operator identity.
topics.explanation: Members are visitor accounts with their own sign-in links, profiles, subscriptions and content-access decisions. Operator accounts control administration. The host currently has no membership enable/disable toggle, so its enabled fact is unavailable; it does not mean every page requires sign-in or that a member-login widget exists. Verify registered login/access capabilities before promising them. Never use operator sessions or role checks as a substitute for member access rules.

topics.title: SEO
topics.summary: Inspect resolved site defaults and per-entry overrides before publishing.
topics.explanation: SEO metadata affects titles, descriptions, canonical links, sitemaps and social previews. Read current settings and entry metadata, preserve useful imported descriptions, and verify generated HTML with fetch_published_page. A local publication and a successful live deployment are separate facts; check the actual live host before claiming that external crawlers see the update.

topics.title: Deploy
topics.summary: Choose between content publishing, static hosting and server deployment.
topics.explanation: Publishing a draft makes it visible on this Tovu instance. Sending content to another Tovu site, publishing a static export, and deploying the Tovu server use different tools and native host configuration. Discover enabled target capabilities; a turned-on hosting plugin is not proof a host account is connected. Preview before publishing, keep credentials in their existing secure owner, and verify the target live URL after the operation.

workflows.title: Publish the static site to a host
steps: Discover installed hosts: deployment_get_static_publish_capabilities includes disabled hosting plugins, their pluginId, enabled state and how to turn them on. This is the installed inventory, not every possible host. Credential configuration and readiness are separate; an unchecked credential state is unknown. Enable the chosen plugin, then check capabilities again. Do not guess from memory.
Pick the host with the person. Use what they already have: 'my Netlify' means Netlify. Each host's own plugin has its token steps and failure messages.

No credential saved? The person saves it themselves in Admin, Deployment, Static site, or through credential_save's secure card. Never ask them to paste a token into chat, and never put one in a tool argument.
Preview first, always: deployment_preview_static_publish publishes nothing. Tell the person what will be published and where.
Publish with deployment_execute_static_publish. It shows the person a confirmation card; nothing is uploaded until they confirm.

Report honestly. ok: true means the public URL answered. ok: 'partial' means the host accepted the files but the URL is not reachable yet: say so, give the URL, suggest checking again in a minute. Never call it failed, and never call it live.

topics.title: Plugins
topics.summary: Check installation and activation in both plugin families.
topics.explanation: Site/runtime plugins extend site behavior; agent plugins teach the assistant and may contribute tool, provider or guide surfaces. Installed and enabled are different states. Read live inventory and use host capability lookup to ask whether another plugin is present; never import another plugin. Disabling How Tovu works removes its enrichment while core site_guide cards and live facts continue working. Tool pointers are discovery hints, not permission grants.

topics.title: Jini packages
topics.summary: Reuse shared @jini-ai capabilities before adding generic code.
topics.explanation: Jini packages own generic agent execution, tool authorization, chat, MCP, OAuth, CMS primitives and platform services. Tovu owns CMS/site policy and thin adapters. Inspect the installed package exports and actual behavior owner before extending them; do not copy a sibling lifecycle or bypass dependency inversion. Public boundaries take required and optional objects, and host effects enter as ports. Another product supplies its own guide cards without importing Tovu.
